correctness.rationale: Every Hilbert (1,d,1) graded commutative local Gorenstein algebra is controlled by a nondegenerate symmetric multiplication form B. Its nonzero maximal-ideal vertices consist of q-1 socle elements of degree q^(d+1)-2 and q lifts of each nonzero v. Distinct nonzero v have q^d possible zero-product partners, with the self-loop removed iff B(v,v)=0, giving degrees q^d-2 (isotropic) and q^d-1 (anisotropic). The classical finite-field quadratic Gauss-sum/characteristic-two linear-square formulas for Z(B), plus finite-field similarity classification, distinguish both even-dimensional similarity classes and yield unique odd-dimensional class. Recovering q,d,Z(B) recovers ring isomorphism type, including finite field automorphism ambiguity. Independent complete degree enumeration corroborated cases q=2,3,5 and alternating/nonalternating split.
risk: Precisely standard graded Gorenstein Hilbert (1,d,1), d>=2 over finite fields; not general Artinian Gorenstein rings. Finite tests verify only small primes/dimensions.

value.rationale: A full degree multiset is a coarse, natural graph invariant. Recovering the residue-field order, embedding dimension, and symmetric form similarity yields a nontrivial inverse rigidity theorem for a geometrically natural Gorenstein ring family, distinguishing even-characteristic alternating forms from nonalternating ones. This solves the graph-isomorphism-to-ring-isomorphism question throughout the stated family, beyond familiar form-counting inputs.
risk: Not a theorem for all graded local algebras or all finite Gorenstein rings; potential older equivalent graph rigidity needs ongoing priority vigilance.

limitations: Field size any prime power, d>=2; grading and one-dimensional socle hypotheses essential.
Isomorphisms may act semilinearly on residue fields; finite-field automorphisms preserve relevant isotropic similarity types.
